bounded_statement: For the selected result in results/report.md (Welch's two-sample t-test on 48 aliquots, t = 12.84, df = 45.0, p < 0.0001), the workflow enters all four repeated aliquot rows from each of the 12 starter jars into scipy.stats.ttest_ind as if each row were an independent observation, reporting n = 24 per flour group and df = 45.0, even though the data description designates jar_id as the independent unit and states the four aliquots per jar are measurements of the same batch; there are only 6 independent jars per group, so the reported degrees of freedom and precision are inflated roughly fourfold relative to a jar-level analysis.

counterevidence_considered.description: The report transparently labels its counts as aliquots rather than claiming 48 independent starters, and a jar-level reanalysis (jar means: rye 9.4, 9.8, 10.0, 10.2, 10.4, 10.2 vs wheat 8.2, 8.4, 8.6, 8.6, 8.8, 9.0; Welch t ~ 7.5 on ~10 df) would still be highly significant, so the direction of the substantive conclusion is not an artifact of the pooling. However, this does not negate the issue: the selected result makes a jar-level substantive claim about starters while its reported t, df, SDs, and sample sizes are computed by entering the 4 correlated aliquot rows per jar into ttest_ind as independent observations.
counterevidence_considered.observed_value: conclusion direction robust to jar-level aggregation; reported statistics are not

evidence.description: read_groups() pools every row's acidity_ml into a flat list keyed only by flour_type; jar_id is never read, so repeated aliquots from the same jar enter the pooled sample as separate observations.
evidence.observed_value: groups keyed by flour_type only; jar_id ignored

evidence.description: The pooled per-aliquot lists are passed directly to scipy.stats.ttest_ind, a procedure whose validity assumes each entry is an independent observation.
evidence.observed_value: ttest_ind applied to 24 rye and 24 wheat aliquot values

evidence.description: The input data contain four rows per jar (shown here for jar R01), confirming repeated entries per independent unit flow into the pooled samples.

The report states per-group sample sizes of 24 aliquots and the selected result claims df = 45.0 on 48 aliquots, reflecting the aliquot-level (not jar-level) sample size; only 6 independent jars exist per group.

source_refs.quoted_text: [selected-result] Welch's two-sample t-test on 48 aliquots shows that rye-refreshed starters reach a higher titratable acidity than wheat-refreshed starters, by 1.400 mL of 0.1 M NaOH (t = 12.84, df = 45.0, p < 0.0001).

extensions.x-stage1-falsification-attempt: I attempted to falsify the issue three ways. (1) I checked whether the workflow aggregates to one value per jar before testing: it does not; read_groups() never reads jar_id and appends every row's acidity_ml directly, and no other function touches jar_id. (2) I checked whether aliquots could legitimately be treated as independent units: the data description rules this out explicitly ('four measurements of the same batch of starter, not four separate batches') and names jar_id as the independent unit column. (3) I checked whether the selected result confines its claim to aliquot-level description only: it does not; it asserts that 'rye-refreshed starters reach a higher titratable acidity than wheat-refreshed starters' — a claim about jars/starters — while citing df = 45.0 derived from treating 48 correlated aliquot rows as independent (correct jar-level df would be ~10 with 6 jars per group). I also verified arithmetically from data/input.csv that the reported group means (10.000, 8.600), n = 24 per group, and the fourfold inflation of per-group sample size (24 aliquots vs 6 jars) are consistent with pooling all rows. All falsification attempts failed, so the issue stands as demonstrated.

root_cause: read_groups() in workflow/analysis.py keys the data only by flour_type and appends every row's acidity_ml to a flat per-group list, never reading or aggregating over jar_id; these pooled lists of 24 values per group (4 correlated aliquots x 6 jars) are then passed directly to stats.ttest_ind, a row-independent procedure, so within-jar repeated measurements are treated as independent replicates.
